title: You Will Receive the Crown of Glory
story:
A shepherd cared for a small flock of sheep on a hillside.

Every morning, he led them to green grass and clean water.

When the weather became dangerous, he searched for a safe place and kept the sheep together.

Sometimes one sheep wandered away, and the shepherd would patiently search until he found it and brought it back.

The sheep did not always understand the dangers around them, but they trusted the shepherd because he faithfully cared for them.

At the end of each day, the shepherd counted his sheep and made sure they were safely inside the fold.

The Bible often uses the picture of a shepherd to help us understand God's care for His people.

Jesus is the Chief Shepherd, and those who serve His people are called to care for them faithfully and humbly.

Christian service is not about gaining power, recognition, or praise from people.

It is about loving others, guiding them toward Christ, encouraging them when they are weak, and remaining faithful even when the work is difficult.

There may be times when our efforts are unnoticed or when we feel tired from serving others.

But God sees every act of faithful service.

Peter reminds church leaders that when the Chief Shepherd appears, those who have faithfully cared for His people will receive a crown of glory that will never fade away.

This promise reminds us that our reward ultimately comes from God, not from people.

Whatever responsibility God has given you, serve faithfully and with humility.

Even when nobody notices, God sees your faithfulness, and He will never forget the work done for His glory.
life_lesson: Serve God and care for others with humility and faithfulness, not for recognition. The Chief Shepherd sees your service and promises an unfading reward.
prayer:
Dear Heavenly Father,

Thank You for being my Chief Shepherd and for caring for me with unfailing love.

Teach me to serve You and care for others with humility and faithfulness.

Help me not to seek recognition, praise, or position, but to serve with a sincere heart.

Give me patience when people are difficult and strength when serving becomes tiring.

Help me encourage those who are weak, guide those who are searching, and care for those You have placed in my life.

When my work goes unnoticed, remind me that You see everything I do for Your glory.

Keep my heart faithful until the day Christ appears.

Thank You for the promise of an unfading crown of glory.

In Jesus' name,
Amen.
reflection_question:
Are you serving others because you love God, or because you want recognition?

Is there someone God has placed in your life whom you need to encourage or care for more faithfully?

How can you serve with greater humility today, knowing that God sees your faithfulness?
verse: And when the Chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the crown of glory that will never fade away.
